classifiedFindings.title: batchMint missing nonReentrant guard: ERC1155 mint hook enables cross-contract reentrancy (no demonstrated asset loss)

classification.assetImpact: None demonstrated. The mint loop (L257-259) re-enters via onERC1155Received while the contract holds paymentAmount and (when active) the nudge pot, but with no proven non-idempotent value-out path that extracts a third party's funds, the exposure is a missing-guard / reentrant-events condition: a deviation from the project's own stated convention (OZ ReentrancyGuard mandated; sibling NFTStaker guards every entry point), not a realized loss.
attackPath: 1. Attacker deploys a contract recipient implementing onERC1155Received.
2. Attacker (or a front-end) calls batchMint with recipient = attacker contract.
3. nftMinter.mint re-enters batchMint mid-loop via onERC1155Received.
4. WITHOUT a demonstrated cross-frame value extraction, the inner frame's own dust refund nets against its own paymentAmount and self-balances; no third-party asset leaves the contract.
classification.likelihood: low - reentrancy is reachable, but absent a concrete asset-loss leg this is a code-quality / defense-in-depth gap.
classification.assumptions: No third-party funds are present in the contract at callback time, OR the balance-based refund self-nets within a single caller's frames so no extraction occurs.
classification.externalRequirements: none for the missing-guard observation itself.

classifiedFindings.justification: C4: a missing reentrancy guard with no demonstrated asset loss is incorrect state handling / convention deviation = QA/Low. Matches the existing L-01 adjudication. This is the validated floor severity if the PoC does NOT prove cross-party extraction.
classifiedFindings.humanReviewFlag: Floor branch. Do NOT overwrite L-01 status (submitted). Severity stays Low unless CLASS-001b is activated by a passing Tier-3 PoC.

classifiedFindings.title: batchMint cross-contract reentrancy steals an in-flight third-party payment via the balance-based dust refund
classifiedFindings.plausibility: plausible (conditioned on PoC + in-scope third-party funding trigger)

classification.assetImpact: Direct theft of a third party's funds. The dust refund at L287-289 sends remaining = paymentToken.balanceOf(this) to the CURRENT frame's msg.sender. A re-entrant inner frame (attacker as msg.sender) reads a balance that still includes an OUTER honest caller's unspent paymentAmount and/or donated funds, and carries it to the attacker. Balance-based, non-idempotent across frames.
attackPath: 1. Third-party funds are present in the contract (e.g. BalancerPoolerV2 donates USDC into it; or an outer honest batchMint's paymentAmount is in-flight).
2. Attacker contract is the recipient and implements onERC1155Received.
3. nftMinter.mint(_dispatcherIndex, recipient) fires onERC1155Received mid-loop (L257-259), before the outer frame reaches its refund.

4. The inner attacker frame runs its own batchMint to completion and hits L287-289, where remaining = balanceOf(this) includes the outer/third-party balance; safeTransfer sends it to the attacker (msg.sender of the inner frame).
5. Attacker extracts funds that were never theirs; the outer accounting is left short.
classification.likelihood: medium-to-high once the funding trigger holds - no special privilege; any attacker can be a contract recipient and front-ends batch-mint to arbitrary recipients.
classification.assumptions: A non-idempotent cross-frame extraction is demonstrated by the PoC (balance-based refund sweeps an outer/donated balance to the inner attacker frame).
classification.externalRequirements: Third-party funds must be in the contract at callback time. Cited trigger (BalancerPoolerV2 USDC donation; front-end batch-minting to a contract recipient) is OUTSIDE this submodule and MUST be validated as in-scope-rooted and NOT a known-invalid integration/user mistake before the High stands.

classifiedFindings.justification: C4 High: assets can be stolen via a valid attack path with no hand-wavy hypotheticals, executable by any external attacker, direct protocol compromise. The C4-style caveat is the external funding requirement (donated/in-flight third-party balance) which is documented as an external requirement; combined with a confirming PoC the impact is direct theft = High. Without the PoC OR if the trigger is a known-invalid integration mistake, fall back to CLASS-001a (Low).
classifiedFindings.humanReviewFlag: ACTIVATE ONLY on a passing Tier-3 PoC demonstrating cross-party extraction AND validation that the out-of-submodule funding trigger is in-scope-rooted. Otherwise the floor (CLASS-001a, Low) is authoritative. Severity flip must not be auto-committed; /ledger disposes.

classifiedFindings.title: Residual MEV / winner-take-all nudge-pot capture after the minReward partial fix (residual of M-01)

classification.assetImpact: No direct theft from a protected user: the minReward floor (L278-280) lets an honest claimer revert if the deliverable reward is below their stated minimum, so a front-run loser is made whole (mints + payment roll back atomically). The residual is incentive-budget value leaking to MEV - the nudge pot (a protocol-funded incentive) is captured by whoever wins the mempool race rather than reaching the intended participant, a protocol-intent mismatch.
attackPath: 1. Owner funds the nudge pot; an honest user broadcasts a batchMint with count >= nudgeSize expecting the pot.
2. A front-runner observes the mempool and submits a batchMint that meets the threshold with higher priority fee.
3. The front-runner's frame reads nudgeAmount = balanceOf(this) (L271) and is paid the full pot (L282-285).
4. The honest user's tx either reverts on the minReward floor (protected, no loss) or, if they set minReward = 0, mints and receives nothing (see CLASS-003).
5. The incentive budget is captured by MEV; protocol intent (reward the intended participant) is defeated.
classification.likelihood: medium - requires a funded pot and a public mempool; standard MEV conditions, no special privilege.
classification.assumptions: Nudge pot is funded and the feature is active (nudgeSize != 0, nudgePaymentToken set). The honest claimer sets minReward > 0 (else this degrades into CLASS-003's silent loss).
classification.externalRequirements: Public mempool / orderable transactions; a funded incentive pot. No direct user-fund theft - loser is refunded by revert.

classifiedFindings.justification: C4 Medium: assets are NOT at direct risk (the minReward floor protects the honest spender), but the protocol's intended function (delivering the incentive pot to the intended participant) is impacted and value leaks to MEV with stated assumptions (funded pot, public mempool) and external requirements (orderable txs). This is squarely the C4 'leak value with a hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements' band. Confirms the M-01 Medium as a narrowed residual; NOT downgradable to Low because the leaked amount is the full pot (a real incentive-budget amount, not dust) and the function impact is concrete.
classifiedFindings.humanReviewFlag: Residual of an ACKNOWLEDGED finding - do NOT re-report as new, do NOT overwrite M-01's acknowledged status, do NOT mark fixed. story-015 minReward is a correctly-implemented PARTIAL mitigation (loser-overpay leg only); the pot-capture leg persists at Medium.

classifiedFindings.title: minReward == 0 backward-compatible default silently opts out of the slippage fix (integration footgun)

classification.assetImpact: Indirect and conditional: minReward = 0 always clears the floor (L278: any reward, including 0, passes), so an integrating UI that omits the param re-exposes the honest caller to M-01's loss (spend the payment, win no pot). The loss is realized only when the user is independently front-run (CLASS-002), and it stems from a caller/integrator-supplied parameter default, not a protocol-side theft path.
attackPath: 1. An integrating UI calls batchMint and omits / defaults minReward to 0.
2. The slippage floor (L278-280) is inert for that call.
3. If the user is then front-run (CLASS-002), the user mints, pays, and receives an empty pot with no revert protection.
4. The user silently overpays - the exact scenario story-015 was meant to prevent.
classification.likelihood: low - requires an integrator to ship the unsafe default AND the user to be front-run; the safe value exists and is one parameter away.
classification.assumptions: Integrator omits minReward; user is subsequently front-run.
classification.externalRequirements: Off-submodule integrating UI behavior; combines with CLASS-002's mempool conditions to realize loss.

classifiedFindings.justification: C4 QA/Low: this is a spec-usability / opt-in-default footgun (the slippage guard exists but the backward-compatible default bypasses it), not a protocol-side asset-loss path. The loss only materializes through a separate Medium (CLASS-002) AND an integrator mistake. Per C4 'user input mistakes' and integration-default footguns are QA-band; the protocol code is functioning as written and the safe value is available. Confirms the econ-scanner Low. Worth flagging in the QA report as a recommendation to default minReward conservatively or require an explicit acknowledgement.
